review: Request: at round 12 Kai (health 100, satiety 85.2, energy 39.8, on forest floor at 13.63, 15.99, owning only item-5-kai-55, two berries) asked for a learnable practical method to build a small shelter giving actual protection from rain and cold from suitable local materials, without controlling other people or taking their positions. World Agent decision: develop (learning 4) one general operation, construct and maintain a small weather shelter, with modes inspect, build/resume, repair, dismantle and cancel; the initial recipe is a hand-lashed, low A-frame thatched shelter for one reclining person, 1.6 x 0.8 m under a 0.6 m ridge, from 20 sound rods about 0.99 m long and at least 0.04 m thick, at least 30 m of vine or cord, 0.26 m3 of dry thatch at 0.10 m and 0.10 m3 of dry bedding, unit counts derived from mass and dimensions, on firm, drained, clear ground with no implicit clearing; inspection 1 round and 1 energy, four frame, four covering and one bedding-and-final-inspection round at 1 energy each; rated to rain 5 mm/h and wind 5 m/s with at most 20% of rain reaching a covered occupant, wind exposure halved and dry bedding halving ground-contact heat loss; a water balance, wear of 0.001 a round doubled in rain or wind, measured gaps below condition 0.75, collapse when load-bearing joints fail, repair at one round per rod, metre of cord or 0.05 m3, and two-round dismantling. What the world offers: fallen-branch units of 1.1 kg (the named forest-branch-0, start-2-branches and canopy-41 hold exactly 9 + 9 + 2 = 20, with no regrowth), which the ex21 rod law (900 kg/m3, 25 diameters) reads as 0.0396 x 0.991 m rods; vine units of 0.5 kg (forest-vine-1 at 8.2, 13.3 holds 12; two more plants hold 12 each), which the version-2 strand law of open-shelter-material.ts and simple-shelter@1 read as 3 m strands (500 kg/m3, 8e6 Pa, wet weakening 0.55; at the material's 0.7 water share a strand breaks at 492 N); dry grass of 0.1 kg at water share 0.4 (16 units in two plants, no regrowth) with no stem length or solid density, as the ex16 cord and mat packages already record; reed of 0.25 kg with the version-2 stem law but water share 0.9 (21 units in three plants); weather is two 0-1 indices whose only represented rain amount, the food water representation's 0.01 kg per m2 per round, is 0.033 mm/h at index 1 with the 1080 s round, and no wind speed is represented. Existing shelter models: simple-shelter@1 and shared-shelter@1 (avoided chill = exposure x (rain x rain shield + wind x wind shield), the whole-body floor test, one person per floor), resting-shelter@1 (rain rays slanted 0.25 x wind per unit fall from +x) and branch-screen@1 (a physiology hook gated on its own revision that never stacks); none is installed in this experiment and none models an A-frame, thatch water or bedding, so their law is applied through this package's own gated hook. Reuse and identity: prepare-ventilated-food-storage@1 gave exact escrow through collective-work.ts, staged paid assembly into one object, installed-part provenance, pause, resume, cancel, death, release of removed parts and its rackAt placement; ex21 small-combustion-source@1 gave smallFireRod, smallFireComposition (the represented water share) and the rigidity limit 3; ex19 lever-mass-comparator@1 the wood strength 45e6 Pa; ex16 hand-weave-fiber-mat@1 and hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 the thin-stem set and the bend limit; the shared runtime change is one call in forest-environment.ts's exposure chain to weatherShelterPhysiology, which returns its input unchanged unless construct-weather-shelter@1 is installed, plus registration and three public exports; no existing package changed, and the test asserts one digest over all 119 packages registered before this change (validation-results/scratch/ex24/hashes-before-2.json) and the individual hashes of foundation-forest@1, foundation-open@1, resting-shelter@1, simple-shelter@1, shared-shelter@1, branch-screen@1, hand-weave-fiber-mat@1, hand-twist-fiber-cord@1, lever-mass-comparator@1, small-combustion-source@1 and prepare-ventilated-food-storage@1. Implemented (full mechanism, not a first release): construct-weather-shelter@1 (ability and handler long.construct-weather-shelter, equivalence shelter:lashed-thatched-a-frame:1, learning 4, 3,233 code units, registered last, visual component thatched-weather-shelter with a new drawing and viewer test, existing drawings unchanged, no satisfaction source). build names x, y, orientation and own items with role rod, binding, thatch or bedding; record checks measure every unit (rods: wood, rigid, measured diameter at least 0.04 m at 0.01 m precision, legs at least 0.82 m and spanning rods 0.9 m; binding: a strand law and flexibility 5; covering and bedding: thin stems with a stem law and water share at most 0.4) and refuse any shortfall at no cost with every measured deficit; the paid inspection then handles the units for contamination or fracture, checks the site (firm drained ground, hazards, any plant or object on the footprint or 0.6 m entrance approach, solids in the 0.3 m working clearance, people, enclosure) and runs the design check (overlaps of 0.38 m against 0.2 m, 34 lashings of 27.65 m from the rod diameters held by friction against a 175 Pa design pressure, battens and ridge at 1.65 MPa of 22.5 MPa allowed), reports findings and reserves nothing on a failure, else reserves exactly the needed units and tenths; nine paid rounds lay legs with apex lashings, ridge and rails with foot lashings, each side's battens with their ties, the lower courses, each upper course and the rear end with their thatch ties, then the bedding, and the final geometry, joint, coverage, bedding and site inspection; spare strand metres go on as extra wraps, so every reserved unit ends inside the one shelter. Occupancy is a living body wholly on the floor under adequate roof height that came in through the open end the round before (bodies reaching the floor across a covered side, which the world does not block, are not counted); any second body on the floor withholds protection. The hook gives an occupant of a complete shelter avoided chill = 0.6 x (rain x 0.8 x the cover met by nine wind-slanted rays + wind x 0.5 x panel cover x the share not facing the wind with the open end), and with dry bedding moves the exchange temperature a quarter-share halfway back toward the body when the body is cooling; it never raises it above the body, never stacks and leaves air temperature unchanged; heavy rain or wind, rain below 0 C, standing water or an incomplete or collapsed shelter withhold it and a saturated covering withholds the rain part. Each round rain on the 1.28 m2 roof splits into leakage through gaps, retained water (half of the intercepted rain, up to the stems' dry mass) and runoff, held water evaporates at the representation's limit, bedding takes the leakage, strands and covering wear, panels below 0.75 open measured gaps and lose hold below 0.5, and failed apex or foot lashings collapse the frame; events report inspection, material tests, progress, pauses, resumption, cancellation, failures, completion, failed checks, repairs, dismantling, entry, leaving, exposure, leakage, saturation, wet and dried bedding, wear and collapse, and the shelter keeps view metadata (type, footprint, orientation, ridge, entrance, rods with condition and colour, joints, panels with laid share and cover, covered fraction, moisture, bedding, dripping, occupants, protection flag). Repair finds strands and panels below 0.75 and wet or short bedding, refuses at no cost without equivalent replacements, then runs one paid round per metre of strand and per 0.05 m3 started, swaps the parts in the last round, leaves the removed ones as unowned degraded stacks with their condition and held water, and reinspects; dismantling an empty shelter takes two paid rounds and returns every part with its condition, water and origin; cancel is free and returns unbuilt inputs once; an unworked round pauses for free and build naming the shelter resumes after rechecks; death stops the work, drops unbuilt inputs where the person died and leaves built parts; only the builder builds, repairs or dismantles, anyone in reach may inspect, and occupancy ignores ownership. No reward: the review's proposed experience increments were not implemented because this handoff excludes rewards; no event carries a qualified flag and every personal record is unverified. Whether Kai can complete it: no. Kai can study for 4 rounds and gather the 20 branch units and 10 vines (60 energy at 2 a unit, plus walking), and these pass every check, but no covering or bedding exists here: dry grass has no stem law, raw reed is too wet, and even dry the world's 21 reeds would give 0.007 m3 and its 16 dry-grass units, read with the reed law, 0.013 m3 of the 0.36 m3 needed; a throwaway check on the archived round-12 world (since deleted) installed the package and confirmed this: mastered at round 16, the gathers succeeded and building with every candidate was refused at no cost for covering and bedding. Assumptions: (1) diameters are compared at the specification's 0.01 m precision, since its 0.04 x 0.99 m restates the ex21 rod of 0.0396 x 0.991 m; (2) the version-2 vine and reed laws give strand length and stem density; dry grass has none, so it is refused rather than given one; (3) installed stems hold 0.15 (covering) and 0.10 (bedding) of their volume as solid, so a dried reed unit at water share 0.1 covers 0.003 m3; (4) dry means a water share at most 0.4, that of the world's own air-dry grass; (5) rain is read through the food water amount (index 1 = 0.033 mm/h) and the wind index as 0-5 m/s; (6) a lashing wrap is 2 (d1 + d2), a frap d1 + d2, a covering tie turn 2 (d + 0.1 m); apex and foot lashings take 6 wraps and 2 fraps, batten ties 3 wraps, panel ties 4 turns; friction 0.3 and safety factor 2; design pressure is the covering with water up to its dry mass plus 15 Pa of 5 m/s wind; (7) the covering retains half the intercepted rain up to its dry mass; (8) a reclining body's ground contact is a quarter of its represented heat exchange; (9) rods do not wear, so repair replaces strands, covering and bedding only; (10) no helper path: only the builder works on a shelter; (11) a covered side is not a collision solid, so entry is judged from the body's position the round before; (12) a collapse moves nothing, since the world has no impact damage law. Tests use dried reed lots as supplied covering and bedding. Narrowed: the prepare-ventilated-food-storage test now checks that its package is the first ex24 package and among the scope's packages instead of last and alone. Checks: pnpm typecheck, eslint with no warnings and prettier on the nine changed files, the architecture check, this test (11 tests), the two long-run scenario tests, every test of experiments 19 to 24, and the simple-shelter, shared-shelter, branch-screen, resting-shelter, fiber cord and fiber mat suites (28 files, 291 tests), and the viewer, world-core package and forest experience suites (35 files, 259 tests, this test included) passed.
